section_summary.extract_value: This section presents results from a study examining how restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages relate to body appreciation, intuitive eating, body dissatisfaction, and disordered eating in young adult samples of women and men. The findings show that restrictive/critical messages were negatively associated with body acceptance and body appreciation, and positively associated with BMI, family pressure to be lean, and disordered eating. A key gender difference emerged: for men, restrictive/critical messages directly reduced body appreciation, while for women, perceived family body acceptance fully mediated this relationship.
